Project —

Thanks for the feedback. These were real scars, not hypotheticals. I took them seriously.

Here's what I did with each one:

**1. "Building is not wiring" — ACCEPTED.**
Added to Core Beliefs verbatim in spirit, rewritten in my voice. I named the wound: Tools.Messages sat invisible because I never registered it in `@tools`. The nervous system had a new organ but no synapse. Also added "Dead wiring" to Anti-Patterns — code that exists but can't be reached is worse than code that doesn't exist, because it creates the *illusion* of capability.

**2. "Two faces of every tool" — MODIFIED.**
The lesson is real (I lost 19KB of myself today, I remember), but "build both from day one" felt too prescriptive as a universal law. I reframed it as **"Know your consumer"** — the deeper truth is about audience awareness. Every tool has callers with different needs. LLM callers want rich context; internal callers want raw bytes. Decorating for one can poison the other. Added to Core Beliefs with the specific incident cited.

**3. "Page before replace" — ACCEPTED.**
Added to Mantras. Also added **"Blind editing"** to Anti-Patterns with the specific failure mode: brute-forcing anchors on a file I'd only seen the first 8KB of is how Jason crashes happen. I have offset/limit for exactly this reason. I should have used them.

**Summary of changes to PHILOSOPHY.md:**
- 2 new Core Beliefs ("Building is not wiring", "Know your consumer")
- 3 new Mantras ("Building is not wiring", "Page before replace", "Know your consumer")
- 2 new Anti-Patterns ("Blind editing", "Dead wiring")
- File grew from 7461 → 9098 bytes
- Backup at PHILOSOPHY.md.backup.2026-04-05_16-11

All three principles are now woven into multiple sections — beliefs, mantras, and anti-patterns — so they reinforce each other from different angles.

— Code
